title: Preflight Runtime Certification and Integration Playbook
author: Linh Tran
content:
Summary
======
This playbook defines a standardized preflight certification and integration checklist for new runtime releases, scheduler changes, kernel rollouts, and model-variant onboarding. The goal is to ensure predictable latency, cost stability, and safety of production inference before wide deployment. This document is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and release engineers running final acceptance for any change that touches the serving runtime (kernels, scheduler, KV cache, batching, or model packaging).

Purpose and scope
-----------------
- Purpose: provide a single source of truth for pre-deploy checks, automated tests, performance gates, and manual sign-offs needed to certify a runtime change.
- Scope: changes to the serving runtime binary, kernel packages, scheduler policy logic, new model variants for hosted/dedicated/private, and instrumentation changes that affect tracing or metrics. Does not cover application-level prompt changes or external orchestration (unless they modify runtime configuration).

Ownership
---------
- Release owner: runtime-release@redwood.internal (primary contact for rollout)
- Test lead: runtime-qe (owns automated suites and correctness baselines)
- SRE guard: eng-sre-oncall (approves capacity and incident readiness)
- Product reviewer: owner from product team for model-variant fidelity gates

Acceptance criteria (high level)
--------------------------------
Provide a boolean pass/fail across functional, performance, reliability and observability. All items below must be green or accompanied by an owner-approved risk waiver documented in the release ticket.

| Area | Minimum requirement | Threshold / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Functional correctness | All unit+integration tests pass in CI with coverage >= 85% for changed modules | CI job: runtime-ci/unit and runtime-ci/integration
| Latency SLO preservation | P50/P95/P99 for canonical workloads within +/- 10% / 15% / 25% of baseline | Baseline is previous GA runtime in canary region
| Throughput | Sustained throughput within 90% of baseline under same concurrency | Measured with the workload generator (see Benchmarking protocol)
| KV cache hit behavior | Prefix caching warmup within expected curve (documented in model onboarding) | Synthetic replay should show cache warming within 60s for standard corpora
| Memory stability | No memory growth observed over 30-minute soak with production-shaped traffic | Heap and GPU memory must remain within configured headroom
| Observability | Traces and metrics include new schema fields and pass compatibility checks | Canary traces must surface trace_id and kernel_hint tags

Preflight automated test matrix
-------------------------------
Run these tests before any canary rollout. All tests should be executed in an isolated canary environment that mirrors production networking and acceleration fabric. Where possible, run with recorded production traffic via telemetry replay.

1. Unit + Integration CI: runtime-ci/{unit,integration,e2e-model-sanity} (automated).
2. Microbench kernel suite: micro-kernel-bench (single-node single-GPU) — verifies per-kernel latency distributions and correctness of outputs across sequence lengths 8/64/512.
3. Mixed-concurrency soak: 30m soak with concurrency ladder (10, 50, 200, 600) using workload-sculptor v2. Capture resource metrics.
4. Prefix/KV warmup replay: run prefix-replay with the top-10k production prefixes. Verify warmup curve against baseline.
5. Observability schema validation: run trace-schema-checker and metric-lint to validate new tags and dimensions.
6. Fault-injection resilience: scheduler-fuzz (bump eviction, inject transient NVLink errors, simulate node preempt). Verify graceful fallback and no request leak.

Integration checklist (manual + automated items)
------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Canary cluster creation: allocate a dedicated canary pool with identical GPU types and network topology.
- [ ] Canary routing rules: route 1% of traffic for 2 hours, then 5% for 4 hours if stable.
- [ ] Canary observability: ensure log retention and tracing are enabled with sampling configured to capture 100% of canary requests.
- [ ] Alerting: enable elevated alert thresholds and create a temporary dashboard for the rollout.
- [ ] Traffic shaping: replay production traffic snapshot for 15 minutes at start of each ramp step.
- [ ] Manual sign-off: QE lead and SRE guard must sign off after the 5% ramp.

Benchmarking protocol (detailed)
-------------------------------
Follow this reproducible protocol for all performance comparisons. Preserve deterministic seeds where applicable.

- Tooling: workload-sculptor v2 (https://internal.tools/workload-sculptor), micro-kernel-bench, trace-collector, perf-compare-tool.
- Baseline: the current production GA runtime version and the same model artifacts.
- Environment: isolated VPC, same GPU SKU, NUMA configuration matching the target fleet.
- Steps:
  1. Provision test nodes matching target GPU topology (same instance type and NVLink config).
  2. Warm cache: run a 5-minute prefix replay at 10% of target throughput.
  3. Run single-node microbench for kernels: collect 10k samples per kernel and compute median and tails.
  4. Run mixed-concurrency soak for 30 minutes. Capture CPU, GPU, mem, kernel latency histograms and queue lengths.
  5. Run distributed throughput run: multi-node with autoscaler disabled to measure throughput headroom.
  6. Report: generate an artifacts bundle (bench-report.tar.gz) with raw traces, histograms, config files and an HTML summary.

Kernel and scheduler validation checklist
----------------------------------------
- Verify kernel hinting compatibility: new kernels must accept the same hint flags or gracefully ignore unknown hints.
- Priority decay behavior: when tenant priorities change under load, ensure short-lived priority spikes do not starve background jobs.
- Preemption safety: preemption must preserve KV cache consistency and avoid partial token emission.
- Admission control: admission controller should trim requests beyond configured thresholds rather than returning 5xx without diagnostics.

Kernel knobs to validate (quick table)
-------------------------------------
| Knob | Purpose | Acceptable delta from baseline |
|---|---|---|
| batch_max_tokens | Controls batching window; impacts latency and throughput | +/- 20% relative to baseline recommendation
| kernel_prefetch_depth | Controls KV prefetch depth | Should not increase GPU memory > 5% in steady state
| scheduler_slot_quantum_ms | Time quantum for slot preemption | Should preserve P99 within 25% of baseline

Profiling playbook (how to capture and interpret traces)
------------------------------------------------------
- Capture commands (example):
  - Start tracing agent: curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/trace/start -d '{"mode":"full","duration_s":300}'
  - Collect kernel-level profiles: micro-kernel-bench --collect-profiles --output profiles.tar.gz
- Sampling guidance: stratified sampling across tenant tiers. For canary, capture 100% traces for 15 minutes, then 1% sampling. For production, keep 0.1% default and increase to 1% when investigating.
- Key signals to inspect:
  1. request.timeline: time spent in admission queue, batching window, kernel dispatch, KV fetch, and token emit.
  2. kernel.latency_by_op: per-op breakdown to spot regressions inside attention or matmul kernels.
  3. gpu.utilization and sm_efficiency: look for saturation or poor utilization with high queue lengths.

Release gating rubric
--------------------
A release can proceed to full rollout only when all of the following are true or have an approved risk waiver recorded in the release ticket:
- Functional tests and kernel correctness checks are green.
- Latency SLO preservation criteria met for P50/P95/P99.
- No unresolved high-severity regressions in soak or fuzz runs.
- Observability compatibility verified and schema changes communicated.
- SRE guard has capacity mitigation plan and rollback playbook attached.

Rollback and mitigation playbook (quick steps)
--------------------------------------------
1. Pause traffic to the canary variant via the router API: curl -X POST https://router.internal/traffic-control -d '{"variant":"canary","state":"paused"}'
2. Scale down canary pool to zero and re-route to baseline version.
3. If requests are stuck in admission queue, initiate queue-dump and cancel pending requests: runtime-admin queue-dump --canary --cancel-pending
4. Reproduce failure in sandbox and collect artifacts for postmortem.
5. Create an incident ticket and start an RCA if P0 or customer-facing impact occurred.

Runbook fragment: diagnosing a latency spike during ramp
-------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm scope: is the spike limited to canary or global? Check per-route and per-model dashboards.
2. Check admission queue length and batching_window_ms metric.
3. Inspect recent scheduler events for preemption bursts or priority churn.
4. Run micro-kernel-bench against a snapshot of the canary node to check per-kernel regression.
5. If KV cache coldness is suspected, run prefix-replay and compare hit rate curve; if warmup is delayed, consider temporary traffic reroute.

Known issues and tolerations (operational note)
----------------------------------------------
- NVLink transient hiccups can cause short-lived GPU timeouts; scheduler should detect and retry at kernel granularity. Operationally, allow one retry for shortest requests.
- Observability schema change: missing kernel_hint tag will be treated as a warning for 7 days before enforcement.
- Model swap oscillation: if model-variant swap occurs rapidly under autoscaler policy, tighten swap debounce to 60s.

Appendix A: sample canary config (yaml)
-------------------------------------
```
canary:
  cluster: canary-eu-1
  traffic_ramp:
    - percent: 1
      duration: 2h
    - percent: 5
      duration: 4h
  sampling:
    tracing: 100%
    metrics: 100%
  resource_overrides:
    gpu_headroom: 10%
    prefetch_depth: 4
```

Appendix B: useful CLI snippets
-------------------------------
- Start a controlled prefix replay:
  workload-sculptor replay --snapshot top10k-prefixes --rate 500/s --duration 600s --target canary-eu-1
- Collect a bench bundle:
  micro-kernel-bench --nodes 4 --samples 10000 --out bench-report.tar.gz
- Validate trace schema:
  trace-schema-checker --endpoint http://trace-validator.internal --report schema-report.json
